title: Kahn–Kalai expectation-threshold theorem
abstract: Formalizes Tran and Vu's short proof of the Park–Pham theorem resolving the Kahn–Kalai expectation-threshold conjecture. For an ℓ-bounded family of subsets of a finite ground set, it proves the strengthened covering theorem with the explicit constant L = 1000 and derives the threshold bound p_c(F) ≤ K q(F) log₂ ℓ with the explicit witness K = 100000. The supporting library develops finite-set cover cost, level-density, double-counting, binomial-tail, and numeric estimates.

informal.KahnKalai.covering_theorem: If ℓ ≤ N, p lies in [0, 1], and an ℓ-bounded family H has cover cost at least 1/2 - 2^(-(ℓ+2)), then its upset has at least (2/3 + 2^(-(ℓ+2))) choose(N, m) members of cardinality m, where m = floor(1000 p N log₂(ℓ+1)). For m ≤ N this is the corresponding level-density bound; for N < m both cardinalities are zero.
informal.KahnKalai.park_pham: There is an absolute positive constant K such that every ℓ-bounded finite family with ℓ at least two satisfies p_c(F) ≤ K q(F) log₂ ℓ; the proof supplies K = 100000.
